candidates.name: V1 anode particles 3um
candidates.role: reduce anode activation+concentration overpotential at 4C charge (surface area x1.95, solid diffusion length halved) to keep anode surface potential above 0 V

candidates.name: V2 N/P up (neg 85.2->100um)
candidates.role: shallower anode lithiation at charge cutoff raises anode OCP, reducing end-of-CC plating

candidates.name: V3 neg porosity 0.25->0.35
candidates.role: better ionic access in anode lowers electrolyte concentration polarization near the anode during 4C charge

llm_reason: plating mechanism from baseline: anode_potential_v declines through the 4C CC charge and reaches -0.192 V exactly at the 4.2 V cutoff (charge-in only 17.6% SOC); in the cutoff-limited regime anode surface potential at cutoff is phi_neg = phi_pos - V_cell, so anode-side polarization controls how deep the anode is driven before the voltage limit cuts the charge. Anode-side levers reduce plating without worsening charge acceptance: V1 smaller anode particles (kinetics + solid diffusion), V2 higher N/P (anode OCP stays higher), V3 anode porosity (ionic access). Cathode-side improvements are deliberately NOT proposed: lowering eta_pos would lengthen the CC phase and drive the anode deeper at cutoff (worse phi_neg). Electrolyte sigma/D scalar overrides held in reserve (Chen2020 transport is temperature-dependent Nyman2008 functions; a constant override would remove the low-T transport degradation and flatter -20 C retention - only with an honest upper-bound caveat if architecture saturates). Architecture parameter sources: design choices from baseline Chen2020 values (design space, no literature source). exploration_force OFF: 3 targeted variants at the relevant moment, not a forced grid.
